einzeiler: Navigating a heavy news week of natural disasters, national debt, and surveillance.
kurzfassung: The hosts discuss a catastrophic debris flow in Nepal and examine the heavy emotional toll of consuming negative news. They also touch upon mounting national debt, the ongoing conflict involving Iran, and a rise in cities dropping surveillance camera contracts.
stichpunkte: A massive debris flow in Nepal swallowed houses and swept away a border crossing, while a phone warning allowed a school principal to evacuate 900 students just minutes before destruction.
The emotional impact of constant negative news can lead to feelings of hopelessness, prompting people to step away from screens and focus on hobbies.
U.S. national debt has reached 40 trillion dollars alongside growing concerns over treasury yields and fiscal stability.
An estimated 800 U.S. service members have reportedly been wounded in ongoing tensions related to Iran.
A criminal trial involving the killing of children has sparked protests and national debate regarding postpartum psychosis and mental health support for women.
Cities across the United States are terminating contracts for automated license plate reader and surveillance cameras due to mounting privacy concerns and misuse.

kapitel.titel: National Debt and the Bond Crisis
Lindsay Clancy Trial and Mental Health

beschreibung:
Michael was tasked with finding something uplifting. He failed. This is what a slow week for good news looks like.
We open on the flooding in Nepal and what you can realistically do when you live in terrain that gives you seven minutes of warning. One school got 14 minutes and everyone made it out.
Then the part nobody wants to say out loud: reading the news is taking something from you. I talk about how I decide what to let in.
National debt past forty trillion. Bonds selling off. Printing money and calling it something else. Blind loyalty to a party instead of judging what is actually being delivered. The Kennedy Center.
Roughly 800 wounded U.S. service members in Iran in six months, the classification that kept those numbers quiet, and a reported airstrike on a wedding.
The Lindsay Clancy verdict that never came.
Cities cancelling Flock camera contracts, 214 jurisdictions pulling them out, officers using the data to track people they should not be tracking.
None of it is a reason to quit.
